content: Crypto implementation pitfalls for WhatsApp multi-device: Noise_XX_25519_AESGCM_SHA256 with WA-specific header/prologue, 3-byte big-endian length framing, protobuf-wrapped handshake messages, XEdDSA certificate chain verification (WA_CERT_ISSUER_SERIAL, leaf bound to handshake server static) — all must be byte-faithful; real-world bug: a Rust port checked only serial linkage and skipped leaf/intermediate signature and validity-window verification, allowing MITM to poison the cached IK key (needed full signature + not_before/not_after validation). Noise handshake variants: XX on cold start, IK on reconnect with cached server static, XXfallback when server rejects IK — clients that only implement XX work but waste RTT; clients that guess wrong break. Media crypto: AES-256-CBC + HMAC-SHA256 with truncated 10-byte MAC and 64KB sidecar chunks (16-byte overlap) — not AEAD, WhatsApp-specific. Double Ratchet needs MKSKIPPED out-of-order key store with bounds (Signal hard-caps 2000 messages/5 DH steps); missing skipped-key handling breaks on out-of-order/lost messages. Signal X3DH: prekey batch 812, refill at <10 remaining, server notification-triggered (WHATSMEOW note: open-source clients never rotate signed prekeys — WhatsApp rotates ~monthly). Academic source: USENIX WOOT'25 Prekey Pogo.
